title: Knowledge transfer intervention to implement standardized assessments for evaluating balance and mobility in physiotherapy routine care for people with neurological disorders: A one-group pre-post study
summary:
Standardized assessments are important for evidence-based practice because they make health conditions measurable – for example, balance after a stroke. However, they are still rarely used in German physiotherapy, even though guidelines recommend them. Bringing research into clinical practice is often challenging. International studies show that implementation is more successful when it is based on theory. So far, there is a lack of data on this in Germany.

The aim of the study is to test an intervention developed together with physiotherapists to introduce assessments for evaluating balance and mobility in people with neurological conditions. In preparation, the “De Morton Mobility Index” (DEMMI) was selected as the primary assessment, supplemented by five optional tests. A survey identified factors that facilitate or hinder their use. Based on these findings, strategies were developed to support implementation in practice.

The study now examines these strategies using a pre-post design with therapists from 11 healthcare facilities.
conditions: While the assessments to be implemented are intended for use with individuals with neurological conditions, the evaluation of the study focuses on the behavior change of the participating therapists.

interventions.name: The aim of the study is to conduct and evaluate an implementation intervention developed using participatory and theory-based approaches in order to promote the use of assessments in routine physiotherapy care for people with neurological conditions within a multi-center study involving 11 facilitie

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants work as (physio-)therapists treating individuals with neurological conditions and impairments in balance and mobility.
Exclusion criteria:
Therapists not treating people with neurological conditions.
